barkcrushed-handbook-text: Dried tanning bark, ground on a quern into a coarse powder. Grinding concentrates its tannin.
bark-generic-handbook-text: Ordinary bark, stripped off a log on the sawhorses whenever the strip yields no special bark. A pit kiln takes it in place of gathered sticks, accepting only the ordinary kind. It can be stacked on the ground.
bark-tan-green-handbook-text: Fresh tanning bark, stripped off a log on the sawhorses. Left to itself it dries into the dried kind. In a pile on the ground it dries as fast as in your inventory. In a chest it dries four times slower. Keep it near a lit firepit, forge, clay oven or anything else that warms you, in a pile or in a chest, to dry it up to twice as fast as in your inventory.
bark-tan-dry-handbook-text: Dried tanning bark, what the fresh kind turns into once it has dried out. A quern grinds it into crushed tanning bark.
bark-birch-green-handbook-text: Fresh birch bark, stripped only from birch logs. It yields birch tar: pack it into a perforated pot, seal it with clay and fire it in a pit kiln. Left to itself it dries into the dried kind. In a pile on the ground it dries as fast as in your inventory. In a chest it dries four times slower. Keep it near a lit firepit, forge, clay oven or anything else that warms you, in a pile or in a chest, to dry it up to twice as fast as in your inventory.
bark-birch-dry-handbook-text: Dried birch bark, what the fresh kind turns into once it has dried out. Filling a tar pot takes fewer pieces of it than of the fresh kind.
bark-bast-handbook-text: The fibrous inner bark, stripped from the stringy-barked woods.
bark-medicinal-handbook-text: Medicinal bark. Simmer it in a pot with water for bark decoction.
barkbrew-handbook-text: Simmer medicinal bark with water in a clay pot on a firepit to brew the decoction. Spread a bowl of it on cloth, cattail, or bast to make a healing poultice. See the Woodworking overview.
halflog-handbook-text: Half of a log, split lengthwise. Chop it on a chopping block to split it into firewood. It is also a building block. Place it with rightmouse and it becomes a half-log slab, split side out. See also the Woodworking overview.
maul-handbook-text: Laid on a chopping block and struck with the maul, a whole log splits straight into firewood in one pass. Forge a maul head and haft it onto a stick. Keep an axe for felling trees. See the Woodworking overview.
blockdesc-chopper-frame-*: The frame of a mechanically-powered chopper. Install the parts into it to assemble the machine.
chopper-need-arm: Install the arm before the head.
chopperpart-handbook-text: One of the parts used to build the automated chopper. Install it with rightmouse to assemble the machine.
chopperheadhalf-handbook-text: Half of an automated chopper head. Forge two halves of the same metal on an anvil, then join them with a hammer on the crafting grid into a finished head.
chopper-handbook-text: Place the chopper frame, then install its parts with rightmouse in any order: a drive, an arm and an ordinary chopping block as the bed, then a chopper head into the arm. Only the head can be taken back out, with ctrl + rightmouse. The three mechanism parts are fixed once installed, so break the frame to recover them. Drive the assembled frame with an axle from a windmill or water wheel. Load it by hand with rightmouse or through a chute: it takes whatever the hand chopping block takes, and the finished batch is ejected in front. The reduction gearing trades many turns of the shaft for one slow, heavy fall of the axe. A whole log goes straight to firewood here, and the metal the head is made of affects its durability. See also the Woodworking overview.
blockdesc-sawmill-frame-*: The frame of a mechanically-powered sawmill. Install the parts into it to assemble the machine.
sawmill-need-sash: Install the saw sash before the blades.
sawmill-need-crankshaft: Install the crankshaft before the flywheel.
sawmill-blades-installed: A blade kit is already installed.
sawmillpart-handbook-text: One of the parts used to build the automated sawmill. Install it with rightmouse to assemble the machine.
pitsaw-handbook-text: Used on a pair of sawhorses to rip a log lengthwise into planks or support beams; aim at the pair and press toolmode to pick which, and any log serves, barked or debarked. The trestles are built around it. Forge a pit saw blade and haft it onto a stick. See the Woodworking overview.
barkspud-handbook-text: Used on a pair of sawhorses to strip the bark off a log, turning it into a debarked log. Forge a bark spud head and haft it onto a stick. See the Woodworking overview.
choppingblock-handbook-text: Place a log or half-log on the block with rightmouse, then hold rightmouse with an axe to chop it. Take placed wood back with ctrl + rightmouse. {0} {1} The block itself can be burned as fuel. See also the Woodworking overview.
choppingblock-handbook-frag-halflog: A log splits into half-logs that drop off the block; put one back to split it into firewood.
choppingblock-handbook-frag-halflog-atpl: A log splits into half-logs that drop at your feet; put one back to split it into firewood.
choppingblock-handbook-frag-direct: A log splits straight into firewood, which drops off the block.
choppingblock-handbook-frag-direct-atpla: A log splits straight into firewood, which drops at your feet.
choppingblock-handbook-frag-sticks: Firewood goes on the block too, and splits into sticks.
sawhorse-handbook-text: Build a trestle with rightmouse: a stick, a second stick, then a length of rope. Set a second trestle directly beside the first (not diagonally), and the two lock into a working pair. Lay a log or debarked log on the pair with rightmouse, stand at either end and hold rightmouse with a saw to rip it lengthwise into planks or support beams; aim at the pair and press toolmode to pick which, and any log rips into either. {0} Keep holding and the pair feeds itself the next matching log from your inventory, so a whole stack flows through in one go. To strip bark instead, stand at the side rather than an end and hold rightmouse with a bark spud, the tool made for it, or with an axe and a hammer in the offhand. {1} {2} A log can be sawn or stripped, not both; whichever you begin first locks it in. Take the log back with ctrl + rightmouse. It comes back whole while the work is barely started. Once you are well into it the wood is committed, and the same gesture (or breaking a trestle) discards it. See also the Woodworking overview.
sawhorse-handbook-frag-bothsaws: The pit saw is the tool made for it; an ordinary saw serves as well.
sawhorse-handbook-frag-pitsawonly: Only the pit saw rips here; an ordinary saw is turned away.
sawhorse-handbook-frag-nopitsaw: An ordinary saw is the rip tool here.
sawhorse-handbook-frag-debarked: The debarked log drops out beside the pair, so lay it back to rip it into planks or beams like any barked log.
sawhorse-handbook-frag-debarked-atplayer: The debarked log drops at your feet, so lay it back to rip it into planks or beams like any barked log.
sawmill-handbook-text: Place the sawmill frame, then install its parts with rightmouse in any order: a carriage, a saw sash, a crankshaft and feed levers, then a blade kit into the sash. Only the blade kit can be taken back out, with ctrl + rightmouse. The four mechanism parts are fixed once installed, so break the frame to recover them. Drive the assembled frame with an axle from a windmill or water wheel. Feed a log or debarked log into the top, by hand with rightmouse or through a chute; it rips into planks or support beams, and you cycle which with shift + rightmouse on the frame. The metal the blades are made of affects their durability. See also the Woodworking overview.
craftinginfo-woodworking-frag-bark: Stripped bark is a material of its own: tanning bark for tannin, medicinal bark for a decoction. Birch bark packs into a perforated pot, which is sealed onto a clay pot and fired for birch tar.
craftinginfo-woodworking-frag-sawmill: An automated sawmill does the same ripping under mechanical power, hands-off and in a single pass.
craftinginfo-woodworking-frag-chopper: An automated chopper splits logs into firewood under mechanical power, its gearing trading many turns of the shaft for one heavy blow.

blockhelp-tarrig-assemble: Assemble onto an empty clay pot lying on the ground
blockhelp-tarrig-packbulk: Pack a bundle of birch bark
blockinfo-sawmill-nopower: No power, connect a turning axle
blockinfo-chopper-nopower: No power, connect a turning axle

abilitydesc-sawyer: Increases the yield of planks and beams from sawing logs by {0}% and additional {1}% for each level at the forestry skill. Maxed out at {2}%.
abilitydesc-carefulsawyer: Sawing or debarking a log has a chance of {0}% and additional {1}% for each level at the forestry skill to not reduce the durability of your saw or bark tool. The chance is capped at {2}%.
abilitydesc-splitter: Increases the yield of firewood from splitting logs by {0}% and additional {1}% for each level at the forestry skill. Maxed out at {2}%.
abilitydesc-swifthands: Speeds up your rip-sawing on the sawhorses and your axe chopping by {0}% plus an additional {1}% for each forestry level, up to {2}%.
barktar-handbook-text: Hard, resinous tar rendered out of birch bark. Open a fired tar pot to get it. It stands in for resin: most recipes that call for resin take tar instead. For the others, cook tar alone in a clay pot on a firepit to boil it down into resin. See the Woodworking overview.
tarpot-sealed-handbook-text: Lay the sealed pot on the ground, build a pit kiln over it and light the kiln. It comes out as a fired tar pot. Seal one on the rig: an empty clay pot with a bark-packed perforated pot on top, capped with clay. See the Woodworking overview.
tarpot-fired-handbook-text: Hold the fired pot and press rightmouse to pry it open. Out come birch tar, the perforated pot and the receiver, now a dirty clay pot. A pit kiln turns a sealed tar pot into this one. Both vessels can be used again. See the Woodworking overview.
perforatedpot-raw-handbook-text: Fire the raw pot in a pit kiln to get a working perforated pot. Lay it on the ground and build the kiln over it, like any other raw pottery. Its bottom is perforated so that tar can drip through into the pot beneath it. See the Woodworking overview.
perforatedpot-fired-handbook-text: Set a single empty clay pot on the ground, then assemble this pot onto it with shift + rightmouse. The two pots together are the tar rig: bark chars in the upper pot and tar drips into the lower one. Pack the rig with birch bark using shift + rightmouse, or a batch at a time with ctrl + shift + rightmouse. Seal the full rig with clay the same way and it becomes a sealed tar pot. The perforated pot comes back when the fired tar pot is opened. See the Woodworking overview.

ingameerror-tarpot-notfull: Pack the pot full with birch bark before sealing it
ingameerror-tarpot-assemblefirst: Assemble the pot onto a clay pot before sealing it
